question.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $R(\sqrt{2},3,-1)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1.5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $R$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1.5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1.5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
